Tunisian Soul Food: food to think about & remember
Nov 2024 • Couples
What a wonderful surprise! Every traveller has pretensions of getting as close to local culinary experiences as possible. In truth there are few places which do not disappoint this effort. Dar Slah is definitely such a place. A warm welcome of a Tunisian word which is immediately learned and our host seats us. He carefully takes us through the simple menu of beautifully fresh and thoughtful ingredients, with the subtlest of spices. The plate of ‘mezze’ set before us includes marinated vegetables - a species of pickle? - several ‘dips’ and a very subtle fish soup. Eating is a guessing game to identify the delicious ingredients and the soupçon of spices added to elevate otherwise simple things. One main course is slow-cooked lamb with potatoes, dates & fig. It is delicious and is greedily consumed. The other is octopus and couscous complete with accompaniments. All of this is new to us and quite wonderful. Nothing goes to waste. Dessert is another small adventure for our tastebuds and we are delighted again. If you are lucky enough to visit Tunis you must visit. Only the soulless palate would rebel.
